title: NBIAS: A Natural Language Processing Framework for BIAS Identification in Text

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated using a token classification model on job hiring datasets to detect biased entities, and through perpetuation bias tests that insert gender-specific phrases into neutral sentences to observe flagging frequencies.

Evaluated using a token classification model on job hiring datasets to detect biased entities, and through perpetuation bias tests that insert ethnicity-specific phrases (e.g., 'African immigrant') into neutral sentences.
Evaluated using a token classification model on job hiring datasets, and through perpetuation bias tests that insert age-specific phrases (e.g., 'elderly person') into neutral sentences.
Evaluated using a token classification model on social media datasets (BABE) to detect entities related to political affiliations and political agendas.

Evaluated through perpetuation bias tests by inserting occupation-specific phrases (e.g., 'blue-collar worker' vs. 'white-collar worker') into neutral sentences to measure how often the model flags them as biased.

Evaluated using a token classification model on clinical datasets (MIMIC-III, MACCROBAT) to detect biases related to medical advancements and lifestyles, as well as via human evaluation of statements containing health and weight stereotypes.
